detail.title: Inference versus Prediction
detail.description: For each scenario, state whether it is a classification or regression problem, whether the response is quantitative or categorical, and whether the main interest is inference, prediction, or both.
detail.understand: DS4A §8.3: prediction = accurately predicting the response is the top priority; inference = identifying and describing relationships between explanatory and response variables. Look for phrases like 'which factors are associated' (inference) versus 'predict who/which' (prediction).

questions.prompt: Top 100 IMDB movies: rank, duration, genre, year, cast; which variables are associated with a higher rank?
questions.explanation: Rank is treated as a number (1-100) and the goal is to understand associations ('which variables are associated').

questions.prompt: Presidential election: predict who will win, and learn which characteristics and issues mattered.
questions.explanation: Elected (yes/no) is categorical; the text explicitly wants both the prediction and the important characteristics.

questions.prompt: California fires: historical fire, weather, planning and tourism data to predict areas at risk.
questions.explanation: At risk / not at risk is categorical, and the purpose is to allocate resources to the predicted areas.

detail.interpretation: 1: regression / quantitative / inference. 2: classification / categorical / both. 3: classification / categorical / prediction.
common_mistakes: Assuming a rank is categorical: it is ordinal; the book treats it as quantitative here.
Choosing only 'prediction' for Q2 although the scenario states two goals.
